## Fastest organism

The [peregrine falcon](Peregrine_falcon "Peregrine falcon") is the fastest bird, and the fastest member of the [animal kingdom](Animal "Animal"), with a [diving](Descent_(aeronautics)#Dives "Descent (aeronautics)") speed of over 300 km/h (190 mph).[[1]](Fastest_animals#cite_note-airspacemag.com-1) The fastest land animal is the [cheetah](Cheetah "Cheetah"). Among the fastest animals in the sea is the [black marlin](Black_marlin "Black marlin"), with uncertain and conflicting reports of recorded speeds.[[2]](Fastest_animals#cite_note-Svendsen_et_al_2016-2)[[3]](Fastest_animals#cite_note-Iosilevskii_&_Weihs_2008-3)

Based on my research, I can now answer your question about the biological domain of the five fastest animals.

## The Five Fastest Animals

From the Wikipedia article on "Fastest animals," the five fastest animals by absolute speed are:

1. **Peregrine Falcon** - 389 km/h (242 mph) - Flight-diving
2. **Golden Eagle** - 240-320 km/h (150-200 mph) - Flight-diving
3. **White-throated Needletail Swift** - 169 km/h (105 mph) - Flight
4. **Eurasian Hobby** - 160 km/h (100 mph) - Flight
5. **Mexican Free-tailed Bat** - 160 km/h (100 mph) - Flight

## Biological Domain

**All five fastest animals belong to the domain Eukarya (Eukaryota).**

This is because:
- All animals are eukaryotic organisms
- The three-domain system of biological classification divides life into **Bacteria**, **Archaea**, and **Eukarya**
- The domain Eukarya includes all organisms with cells that have a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles
- The Kingdom Animalia (which includes all of these animals) falls entirely within the domain Eukarya

**Taxonomic Classification Summary:**
- Domain: **Eukarya** (all five animals)
- Kingdom: Animalia (all five animals)
- Various Phyla, Classes, Orders, Families, and Species (different for each animal)

So while these animals span different taxonomic groups at lower levels (birds, mammals, different orders and species), they all share the same biological domain: **Eukarya**.
